The effect of increased ease of offshoring on the local job market for native workers is reflected in a statistically significant increase in the **level of immigrant employment** (coefficient = 8016.0063, p-value = 0.0053), but not in the **share of immigrant employment** (coefficient = -0.00277, p-value = 0.320). This suggests that while more immigrants are employed, their proportion of the total workforce may not be significantly affected.
